quarterly_data.signal: Recursion's 10-K: through partnerships with Roche and Genentech, Sanofi, Bayer and Merck KGaA (Darmstadt, Germany), Recursion has secured more than $500 million in upfront and progress-based milestone payments to date, with the potential for over $20 billion in additional milestones before royalties.

quarterly_data.signal: Customer Merck KGaA, Darmstadt, Germany: under the September 2023 Research Collaboration Agreement, Recursion leads AI-driven design, translational and early non-clinical studies to discover development candidates against initially agreed oncology and immunology targets; Merck KGaA paid a $20 million upfront and Recursion remains eligible for up to $674 million in discovery, development, regulatory and sales-based milestones for the three initial programs (up to $113 million in the discovery phase), plus royalties ranging from mid-single-digits to low-double-digits.

quarterly_data.signal: Supplier Tempus AI (data license to Recursion): Recursion's 10-K: Recursion has issued shares of its Class A common stock to Tempus AI in payment for license fees under the Master Agreement between the two companies (the Tempus Agreement) - 7.1 million shares in November 2025, 3.5 million shares in December 2024 and 3.2 million shares in December 2023 - and may issue additional shares under it; the cash flow statement shows $32,000 thousand of shares issued for the Tempus agreement in 2025.

contracts.signal: Recursion's 10-K: under the January 2022 Collaboration and License Agreement (amended July 2023 and December 2023), Recursion uses its AI-driven, end-to-end platform to discover and advance up to 15 novel small molecule programs in oncology and immunology; Sanofi paid a $100 million upfront plus $4 million for the December 2023 expansion. Each program can yield milestones of up to approximately $343 million (up to $193 million research, development and regulatory; up to $150 million commercial), up to approximately $5.2 billion across all 15 programs, plus tiered royalties. In February 2026 Recursion achieved its fifth milestone, a $4 million payment, bringing upfront and milestone payments to $134 million to date.
contracts.value: $100 million upfront + $4 million expansion; up to approximately $343 million per program and approximately $5.2 billion in aggregate milestones; $134 million received to date

contracts.signal: Recursion's 10-K: under the December 2021 Collaboration and License Agreement with Roche and Genentech for small molecule discovery in neuroscience and an oncology indication, Recursion received a non-refundable $150.0 million upfront in January 2022, a $3M oncology option fee in October 2023, a $30 million acceptance fee for its first neuroscience phenomap in September 2024 and $30 million for the Microglia Map in October 2025. players.product: GPU compute and BioNeMo agent toolkit

connects_to.relationship: DGX H100 SuperPOD (BioHive-2) and DGX Cloud compute for Recursion's biology and chemistry foundation models

contracts.signal: Recursion's 10-K: in July 2023 Recursion entered a strategic collaboration with NVIDIA to accelerate development of its AI foundation models for biology and chemistry using its BioHive-1 supercomputer and priority access on NVIDIA DGX Cloud. In May 2024 it completed BioHive-2, an NVIDIA DGX SuperPOD powered by 63 DGX H100 systems with a total of 504 NVIDIA H100 Tensor Core GPUs, increasing computational capacity by over 4X; BioHive-2 ranked number 76 on the Top500 list in 2025. Recursion largely trains its models on BioHive-2, which it says was built in collaboration with NVIDIA.
contracts.units: 63 DGX H100 systems; 504 NVIDIA H100 Tensor Core GPUs

players.product: cloud compute and AI infrastructure for molecular and biological discovery

connects_to.relationship: Google Cloud compute, storage and Gemini generative AI for the Recursion OS

contracts.signal: Recursion's 10-K: Recursion runs a hybrid storage and compute platform, processing data either in its HPC datacenter (BioHive) or in its cloud, partnering with Google Cloud. In October 2024 it announced an expanded collaboration with Google Cloud to explore generative AI capabilities including Gemini models for the Recursion OS, improve data search with BigQuery and scale compute for large inference workflows; OpenPhenom-S/16 was released in Google Cloud's Vertex AI Model Garden in November 2024. Recursion relies on cloud infrastructure services such as Google Cloud and Amazon Web Services to host substantial portions of its technology platforms.
